editorial:
Imagine you are a tired dad just trying to keep your life together after a messy divorce. That is exactly where you meet Detective Collymore. He takes on a case about a girl named Tiffany who died, and at first, everyone says it was just a natural death. But something feels off, and as you watch him dig deeper, you realize he has walked right into a nightmare called Jitters. The movie starts off like a slow police mystery, but it quickly turns into a scary ride that keeps you on the edge of your seat. It has a gritty, dark feel that makes you feel like you are right there in the room with him.

You will love how the tension builds up, and the acting makes Collymore feel like a real person you actually care about. The twists are surprising, though some parts of the middle feel a bit slow. If you love movies that mix a crime story with pure scares, you need to see this.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, you find out that Jitters is actually a parasitic entity that feeds on fear and anxiety. Collymore discovers that Tiffany did not die naturally, but was consumed from the inside out. In a big showdown, he manages to trap the creature using a high-frequency sound device. He barely escapes with his life, but the movie ends with a shot of his own hand shaking, suggesting the entity might still be inside him.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves detective stories with a supernatural twist.
